findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler can no longer be constructed
findings.body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler and only has `pass`, so it does not implement the abstract methods counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and build_occurrence_and_event_data. Instantiating that class raises TypeError. MetricAlertFire.detector_handler still points at it, and Detector.detector_handler constructs the handler with group_type.detector_handler(self). Any processing of a metric_alert_fire detector therefore crashes inside process_detectors (the exception is not caught, so the rest of the detector batch fails too). The previous handler was a concrete DetectorHandler whose evaluate() returned [] and could be instantiated safely.

findings.title: test_dedupe expected occurrence uses the wrong group key
findings.body: TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe builds the expected IssueOccurrence with build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, "val1", 6, ...) but calls evaluate_group_key_value with group_key "group_key" and value 10. build_mock_occurrence_and_event puts the group key into the occurrence fingerprint via build_fingerprint, and IssueOccurrence equality includes fingerprint, so the expected DetectorEvaluationResult cannot equal the value evaluate_group_key_value actually returns. That assertion fails and the dedupe-skip half of the test never runs.

findings.title: Tests build expected occurrences with the wrong evaluated value
findings.body: build_mock_occurrence_and_event ignores its value argument, and several assertions pass a value that is not the one being evaluated. test_state_results_multi_group feeds group_2=10 but builds the expected occurrence with 6 (line 191). TestEvaluate.test_results_on_change evaluates 100 but expects an occurrence built with 6 (line 490). TestEvaluate.test_dedupe evaluates 8 but expects 6 (line 510). Those tests still pass if build_occurrence_and_event_data is called with the wrong value, so the new hook's value argument is not actually checked.

findings.title: evaluate docstring still says it returns a list
findings.body: StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate now returns dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult], but the docstring still says it "returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult". Callers that follow the docstring will treat the return value as a list (index it, iterate results rather than result objects, and so on) and break against the new contract.
